description: An overview of the meaning and functions of government in Tanzania, its three organs, the levels of central and local government, the Union structure, and the importance of separation of powers.

mcq.questionText: What is the most accurate meaning of the term 'government'?

options.text: A group of citizens who pay taxes to the state
The system and people through which a country is ruled and public affairs are managed
A political party that wins the most votes in an election
The total population living within a country's borders

mcq.explanation: Government refers to the institutions and people that exercise authority to make, apply and enforce laws and manage the public affairs of a country.

mcq.questionText: How many main organs make up the Government of Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: The government has three organs: the Executive, the Legislature (Bunge) and the Judiciary.

mcq.questionText: Which organ of government is responsible for making and passing laws?
mcq.explanation: The Legislature, known in Tanzania as the Bunge (Parliament), is the law-making organ of the government.

mcq.questionText: Which organ of government is mainly responsible for implementing laws and the day-to-day running of the country?
mcq.explanation: The Executive carries out and enforces laws and runs the daily administration of the country through the President, ministers and the civil service.

mcq.questionText: Which organ of government interprets the laws and settles disputes?
mcq.explanation: The Judiciary interprets laws, settles disputes and administers justice through the courts of law.

mcq.questionText: Who is the head of the Executive in the United Republic of Tanzania?

options.text: The Speaker of the National Assembly

mcq.explanation: The President is the Head of State, Head of Government and Commander-in-Chief, leading the Executive organ.

mcq.questionText: What is the common name of the Parliament of Tanzania in Kiswahili?
mcq.explanation: The Parliament of Tanzania is known in Kiswahili as the Bunge, which is the legislative organ.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a function of the Legislature?

options.text: Enacting laws and approving the government budget

mcq.explanation: Besides making laws, the Bunge approves the national budget and oversees the work of the government.

mcq.questionText: What does the principle of 'separation of powers' mainly aim to prevent?

options.text: The concentration of all power in one organ or person
The collection of taxes by the state

mcq.explanation: Separation of powers divides authority among the three organs so that no single organ or individual gains too much power.

mcq.questionText: Which two parts make up the structure of the United Republic of Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: The Union was formed in 1964 by joining Tanganyika (Tanzania Mainland) and Zanzibar to create the United Republic of Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes local government in Tanzania?

options.text: The government that controls the armed forces
The level of government that manages affairs at the district, town and village level
The court system that hears appeals
The body that elects the President

mcq.explanation: Local government brings administration closer to the people by managing services and development at lower levels such as districts, towns, wards and villages.

mcq.questionText: Why is it important for the Judiciary to be independent from the other two organs?

options.text: So that judges can also make new laws
So that courts can decide cases fairly without interference
So that the President can control the courts
So that the Judiciary can collect taxes

mcq.explanation: An independent Judiciary can deliver justice impartially and protect citizens' rights without pressure from the Executive or Legislature.

mcq.questionText: Which official presides over the sittings of the National Assembly (Bunge)?
mcq.explanation: The Speaker presides over and maintains order during the debates and sittings of the National Assembly.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a function of government?

options.text: Providing social services such as education and health
Choosing which religion every citizen must follow
Defending the country from external threats

mcq.explanation: Government provides services, security and defence, but it does not impose a religion, since Tanzania guarantees freedom of worship.

mcq.questionText: The arm of government that includes ministers and the civil service is best described as the:
mcq.explanation: The Executive includes the President, Vice President, Prime Minister, Cabinet ministers and the civil service who implement government policy.

fib.questionText: The three organs of the Government of Tanzania are the Executive, the Judiciary and the _____.
fib.explanation: The Legislature (Bunge) is the law-making organ, alongside the Executive and the Judiciary.

fib.questionText: The Kiswahili name for the Parliament of Tanzania is _____.
fib.explanation: The Bunge is the legislative body responsible for making laws in Tanzania.

fib.questionText: The Head of State and head of the Executive in Tanzania is the _____.
fib.explanation: The President leads the Executive and serves as Head of State and Commander-in-Chief.

fib.questionText: The organ of government that interprets laws and settles disputes is the _____.
fib.explanation: The Judiciary administers justice through the courts of law.

fib.questionText: The United Republic of Tanzania is a union of Tanzania Mainland and _____.
fib.explanation: Tanganyika and Zanzibar united in 1964 to form the United Republic of Tanzania.

fib.questionText: The principle that divides power among the three organs so that no one organ becomes too powerful is called separation of _____.
fib.explanation: Separation of powers ensures each organ has its own duties, providing checks and balances.

fib.questionText: The two main levels of government in Tanzania are central government and _____ government.
fib.explanation: Local government operates at lower levels such as districts, wards and villages to bring services closer to the people.

fib.questionText: The officer who presides over the sittings of the National Assembly is the _____.
fib.explanation: The Speaker chairs parliamentary sessions and keeps order during debates.

fib.questionText: The group of ministers who help the President to run the government is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The Cabinet is part of the Executive and advises the President while running the ministries.

fib.questionText: The highest court in the United Republic of Tanzania is the _____ of Appeal.
fib.explanation: The Court of Appeal is the highest court in Tanzania and hears appeals from lower courts.

tf.questionText: Government is the system through which a country is ruled and its public affairs are managed.
tf.explanation: This is the correct meaning of government as the body that exercises authority over a country.

tf.questionText: The Judiciary is responsible for making new laws in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: Making laws is the work of the Legislature (Bunge); the Judiciary interprets and applies the laws.

tf.questionText: The President of the United Republic of Tanzania is the head of the Executive.
tf.explanation: The President heads the Executive and is also the Head of State and Commander-in-Chief.

tf.questionText: The United Republic of Tanzania was formed by uniting Tanganyika and Kenya.
tf.explanation: Tanzania was formed by the union of Tanganyika (Mainland) and Zanzibar, not Kenya.

tf.questionText: The Bunge is the legislative organ of the Government of Tanzania.
tf.explanation: The Bunge (Parliament) is the law-making organ of the government.

tf.questionText: Separation of powers means that all government power is given to the President alone.
tf.explanation: Separation of powers divides authority among the three organs to prevent the concentration of power in one person or organ.

tf.questionText: Local government helps to bring administration and services closer to the people.
tf.explanation: Local government operates at district, ward and village levels so that decisions and services reach citizens directly.

tf.questionText: Maintaining peace, law and order is one of the main functions of government.
tf.explanation: Ensuring security, peace and order is a core duty of any government.

tf.questionText: The Executive includes the civil service that carries out government policies.
tf.explanation: The civil service is part of the Executive and implements the day-to-day work of government.

tf.questionText: An independent Judiciary makes it harder for citizens to receive fair justice.
tf.explanation: An independent Judiciary actually protects fair justice by allowing courts to decide cases without interference.

hoq.questionText: A Member of Parliament drafts a bill, the Bunge debates and passes it, the President assents to it, and later a court applies it to decide a case. Which sequence of organs has acted, in order?
hoq.explanation: The Legislature makes and passes the law, the Executive (President) assents to it, and the Judiciary later applies it in court.

hoq.questionText: Suppose the same group of people made the laws, enforced them and also judged those accused of breaking them. Which principle would be violated and what is the likely danger?

options.text: Freedom of worship, leading to religious conflict
Separation of powers, leading to abuse of power and unfair justice
The Union structure, leading to the breakup of Tanzania
Local government, leading to poor service delivery only

hoq.explanation: Combining all powers in one group violates separation of powers and risks dictatorship, abuse of power and biased justice.

hoq.questionText: Why might creating effective local government councils improve development more than relying only on central government?

options.text: Because local councils can change national laws on their own
Because decisions made closer to citizens better reflect local needs and encourage participation
Because local government replaces the need for the Judiciary
Because central government has no role in providing services

hoq.explanation: Local government identifies and responds to community needs and promotes citizen participation, complementing the central government rather than replacing other organs.
